medications.purpose: Blood pressure control (part of dual therapy)
medications.nice_justification: NG136 step 1 for patients aged ≥55 or Afro‑Caribbean; CCB preferred first‑line

medications.dose: 2.5 mg once daily, increase to 5 mg after 2 weeks, then to 10 mg as tolerated
medications.nice_justification: NG136 step 1 ACE‑I for non‑Afro‑Caribbean adults <55 y or as part of combination therapy

medications.duration: Lifelong – review annually; add only if BP >140/90 after 4 weeks of ACE‑I + CCB
medications.purpose: Add‑on antihypertensive (triple therapy) to achieve target BP
medications.nice_justification: NG136 step 3 triple therapy – indapamide preferred thiazide‑like diuretic

medications.duration: Lifelong – lipid profile review at 3 months then annually
medications.purpose: Lower LDL‑C and reduce cardiovascular risk
medications.nice_justification: CG126/CG188 high‑intensity statin for patients with IHD risk factors; ≥40% LDL‑C reduction target

medications.dose: 100 mg once daily, increase by 100 mg every 2–4 weeks to target serum urate <360 µmol/L (max 300–600 mg daily)
medications.duration: Until serum urate target achieved, then review annually
medications.nice_justification: CG188 recommends allopurinol as first‑line urate‑lowering agent when hyperuricaemia with comorbidities

medications.purpose: Prevent gout flares when starting urate‑lowering therapy
medications.nice_justification: CG188 advises colchicine prophylaxis when initiating allopurinol

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive blood pressure lowering; risk of hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Monitor BP and symptoms after dose changes; adjust if symptomatic

interactions_checked.interaction: Amlodipine increases atorvastatin plasma concentration (~1.5‑fold), raising myopathy risk
interactions_checked.action: Check CK and symptoms of myopathy after 2 weeks; consider rosuvastatin 20 mg if CK rises

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined ACE‑I and thiazide‑like diuretic may increase serum potassium
interactions_checked.action: Check serum K⁺ and renal function 2 weeks after starting indapamide, then 6‑monthly

contraindications.reason: NICE NG136 states no added benefit and increased renal risk
contraindications.alternative: Use either ACE‑I (ramipril) or ARB (losartan) but not both

contraindications.reason: Contraindicated in hypertension and cardiovascular risk (NG136, CG126)
contraindications.alternative: Use paracetamol for pain; short‑course NSAID only with renal monitoring if absolutely necessary

assumptions_warnings: Patient age, ethnicity and exact eGFR not provided – assumed adult, non‑Afro‑Caribbean, eGFR ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m² for initial dosing; renal function will be checked before ACE‑I, indapamide and allopurinol.
Pregnancy status unknown – assumed not pregnant; ACE‑I contraindicated in pregnancy per NG136.
Allergy status not documented – will confirm no hypersensitivity to ACE‑I, statins or allopurinol before prescribing.
HLA‑B*58:01 testing not performed – required if patient of Asian ancestry before allopurinol initiation.
Baseline liver function tests not available – required before high‑intensity statin initiation.
treatment_summary: Start ramipril and titrate to 10 mg while continuing amlodipine 2.5 mg for hypertension; add indapamide 1.5 mg if BP remains >140/90 after 4 weeks. Switch low‑dose simvastatin to high‑intensity atorvastatin 80 mg for cardiovascular risk reduction. Initiate allopurinol 100 mg with dose titration and short‑course colchicine prophylaxis for gout. Monitor BP, renal function, electrolytes, CK and serum urate as per NICE NG136, CG126 and CG188. Provide lifestyle advice for weight loss, diet, exercise, salt restriction and smoking cessation.
